Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) rather than raw Decimal operations.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to match rounding and normalization conventions. Wrap unit prices with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money.
- [rb-0020] Use Decimal constants for monetary rates and fixed fees: Define percentage rates and fixed fees as module-level Decimal constants, never floats, to avoid rounding drift.
  Declare `RATE = Decimal("0.029")` and `FIXED = Decimal("0.30")` at module level and compute `round_money(amount * RATE + FIXED)`. Floats are rejected by the project's `to_money`, so all monetary math must stay in Decimal.
- [rb-0013] Reuse existing money helpers for currency math: When implementing monetary functions, delegate to the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than raw float arithmetic.
  Search sibling modules (invoice.py, adjustments.py) for established money utilities and error types before writing new code. Using to_money/round_money and BillingError kept the implementation consistent with the codebase and passed hidden tests on the first try.
- [rb-0011] Enforce approval thresholds for large refunds: Refunds above 500.00 require a second approver via keyword-only `approved_by=None`, raising BillingError("approval_required") when missing.
  Finance policy FIN-2026-03: amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise `BillingError("approval_required")` if `approved_by` is falsy. Keep the parameter keyword-only with a default so existing callers keep working, and record `approved_by` in the audit entry.
- [rb-0005] Normalize money inputs before sign checks: Convert unit_price via the project's to_money helper before comparing against ZERO, so strings/Decimals are handled consistently.
  Run raw price inputs through the existing money conversion helper (e.g. to_money) first, then compare the normalized Decimal to ZERO for the negative check. This accepts flexible input types while keeping validation correct.
- [rb-0014] Validate numeric inputs via Decimal(str(x)) with explicit bool rejection: Convert user-supplied rates through Decimal(str(value)) and reject bools, catching InvalidOperation/ValueError to raise the domain error.
  Booleans are ints in Python, so check isinstance(x, bool) first. Wrapping Decimal(str(x)) in try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError) handles strings, None, and other junk uniformly, then range-check the Decimal before computing.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers instead of reimplementing rounding
item.description: When a repo already has to_money/round_money utilities, build new monetary functions on top of them rather than writing fresh Decimal logic.
item.content: Before implementing any amount-handling function, grep for existing money helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO, CENT) and import them. This keeps rounding policy and float-rejection behavior consistent across modules and avoids subtle mismatches with hidden tests.

item.title: Validate numeric inputs by converting via Decimal(str(x)) and rejecting bools/non-finite
item.description: Robust numeric validation converts through str to Decimal, explicitly rejects bool and non-finite values, then range-checks.
item.content: Pattern: reject isinstance(x, bool) first (since bool is an int subclass), then Decimal(str(x)) inside try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError), check is_finite(), and finally enforce min/max bounds with a distinct error code. This handles ints, strings, and Decimals uniformly.

item.title: Match the repo's error convention (BillingError with code) for invalid inputs
item.description: Sibling modules raise BillingError(code, message) for invalid operations; new validation should follow the same convention.
item.content: Inspect errors.py and a couple of sibling modules to learn the exception type and code style before writing validation. Use short machine-readable codes (e.g. invalid_rate, rate_out_of_range) and include the offending value as the message, mirroring existing call sites.
